# Independence of transmission where it binds

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> Wherever transmission binds, dropping one dependence of the giver keeps every other premise and finiteness and breaks it; so no law kept by dropping a dependence derives it, and a reading of the exchange with drawing being depending derives it, each needed.

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

Dropping g's dependence on c at step t (Web.drop, World.drop) changes no level, activity, drawing, need or flow, keeps activity needing support (Web.drop_dependent), the seven other premises and finiteness (World.drop_holds, World.drop_finite), and breaks transmission for every δ at any descent whose descendant depends on c (Flow.drop_untransmitted, World.drop_untransmitting). So every world meeting the seven other premises in which transmission binds has a neighbour, one dependence dropped, meeting all but transmission (World.drop_but); the finite hatch and its neighbour are such a pair (World.finiteHatch_pair). The general boundary: a condition on worlds kept by dropping a dependence and implying transmission implies that transmission does not bind (World.vacuous_of_drop_invariant). A reading of the exchange is such a condition: a relatum depends at its first standing step only on what each relatum giving to it drew on at the giving step (Flow.DependsOnDrawn), or took from across it (Flow.DependsOnFed, which gives the first where only active relata take and only from what they draw on, Flow.dependsOnDrawn_of_fed); both are kept by dropping a dependence (Flow.DependsOnDrawn.drop, Flow.DependsOnFed.drop), so finiteness, the seven other premises and the reading of drawing do not give transmission (World.drawn_not_enough). With one law requiring dependence, at the giver, that drawing on c is depending on it (Web.DrawingDepends), the reading gives inheritance (Flow.inherits_of_drawn, Flow.inherits_of_fed). A finite, balanced, dissipative world bounds every level by the total standing at the first step (World.Finite.level_le); with activity needing support and every relatum embodied the need half holds within a bound on levels (Flow.needsWithin_of_embodied), so in a finite world meeting balance, dissipation, embodiment and activity needing support transmission is exactly inheritance (World.transmitting_iff_inherits; with a bound on levels, World.transmitting_iff_inherits_bounded), and the reading with the link gives transmission (World.transmitting_of_drawn, World.transmitting_of_fed), not vacuously: in the finite hatch whose parent also depends on itself all of these hold and transmission binds (World.bearingHatch_derived). Each is needed (World.drawn_and_link_needed): with the parent's dependence on the food dropped from the finite hatch, the reading holds and the link fails (World.drawn_without_link); in novel the link holds of the parent, on which nothing draws, and the reading fails (World.link_without_drawn). No axiom.

Canonical source: [Transmission.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Transmission.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- Independence and the boundary are stated for every world; the derivation needs finiteness, balance, dissipation, embodiment, activity needing support, the reading of drawing and the link, each supplied openly.
- The link (drawing is depending) is sufficient, not necessary: in the finite hatch the parent draws on itself without depending on itself, and transmission holds there.

P84 (work board), following Ren's ‘move towards 100%’ of 12 October 2026. Reading (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation): the seven other premises only limit dependence and never require one; transmission requires the giver's, so it cannot follow from them, and any derivation needs a law requiring some dependence to exist. Drawing being depending is a candidate for such a law; on Ren's delegation it is not adopted as a law of forming (D31). See the integration document §105.

The checker also verifies core purity: the import closure of the core (GenerativeCore, InquirySufficiency, RelationalRenewal, L1–L4 and the root module Becoming) is exactly these 77 modules, every source declaration in it has an empty axiom report (of the constants Lean generates, only the injectivity lemmas of constructors with fields, injEq, depend on propext; no source declaration uses them, and the checker lists them), and it compiles from Lean's prelude alone (the foundation's import Std removed for that run). The author's counterreview is in §105 of the integration note; there is no independent review yet.

Stated for discrete steps and natural-number amounts; independence is stated on worlds in which transmission binds; the link is sufficient, not necessary; the derivation is not for every world, needing finiteness and the listed premises; the need bound is a coarse bound on levels; drawing is depending is declined as a law of forming, on Ren's delegation; the names are the AI's wording, adopted under Ren's naming rule (drop, DependsOnDrawn, DrawingDepends and others).

- drawn_without_link and link_without_drawn: neither the reading nor the link gives inheritance alone. [Transmission.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Transmission.lean)
